questions.enonce_markdown:
Using the following elements complete the table below:

| Group | Element | General name |
|---|---|---|
| I | ......... | ......... |

*[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
| Group | Element | General name |
|---|---|---|
| I | Sodium, Na | Alkali metals |

(Calcium and magnesium are in Group II, the **alkaline earth metals**.)

questions.enonce_markdown: Give one physical property of the group I metals. ......... *[1 mark]*
questions.corrige_markdown: Any one of: they are **soft** (cut with a knife) and shiny when freshly cut; they have **low melting points** and **low densities** (lithium, sodium and potassium float on water); they are good conductors of heat and electricity.

questions.enonce_markdown: Give one chemical property of the elements of group I. ......... *[1 mark]*
questions.corrige_markdown: Any one of: they **react vigorously with cold water** to give hydrogen and an alkaline solution of the metal hydroxide; they tarnish quickly in air (react with oxygen); they react with chlorine to form ionic chlorides; they form $+1$ ions by losing their single outer electron.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Write equations to show how these elements behave in water.

Na .........

Mg ......... *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Sodium** reacts vigorously with cold water:

$2\mathrm{Na(s)} + 2\mathrm{H_2O(l)} \rightarrow 2\mathrm{NaOH(aq)} + \mathrm{H_2(g)}$

**Magnesium** reacts only very slowly with cold water, but burns in steam:

$\mathrm{Mg(s)} + \mathrm{H_2O(g)} \rightarrow \mathrm{MgO(s)} + \mathrm{H_2(g)}$

(with cold water, very slowly: $\mathrm{Mg(s)} + 2\mathrm{H_2O(l)} \rightarrow \mathrm{Mg(OH)_2(s)} + \mathrm{H_2(g)}$).

questions.enonce_markdown:
(i) Identify a compound of sodium and chlorine commonly used in our homes. .........

(ii) State the bond type in the compound in e (i). ......... *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
(i) **Sodium chloride, NaCl**, common salt (table salt, used in cooking).

(ii) **Ionic (electrovalent) bond**: sodium transfers one electron to chlorine, giving $\mathrm{Na^+}$ and $\mathrm{Cl^-}$ ions held together by electrostatic attraction.

questions.enonce_markdown:
In the laboratory preparation of a gas, X, NaCl, conc.$\mathrm{H_2SO_4}$ and $\mathrm{MnO_2}$ are mixed:

(i) Identify gas X ......... *[1 mark]*

(ii) What is the function of $\mathrm{MnO_2}$: ......... *[1 mark]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
(i) Gas X is **chlorine, $\mathrm{Cl_2}$**. Concentrated sulphuric acid and sodium chloride first give hydrogen chloride, which is then oxidised: $2\mathrm{NaCl} + 3\mathrm{H_2SO_4} + \mathrm{MnO_2} \rightarrow 2\mathrm{NaHSO_4} + \mathrm{MnSO_4} + 2\mathrm{H_2O} + \mathrm{Cl_2}$.

(ii) $\mathrm{MnO_2}$ is the **oxidising agent**: it oxidises the chloride ions (hydrogen chloride) to chlorine gas, and is itself reduced to $\mathrm{Mn^{2+}}$.
